changes: Folder completion includes selected-quality detail, canonical edits per input mip and edited thumbnails; compatible visible/native consumers share the decoder.
Settled edits reuse the existing lossless fp32 cache, complete recipe/source/input identity and common writer; bounded retry for disk contention.
Writer sublimit is min(global budget / 4, 2048 MiB), unchanged disk/temporary quotas. Optional native edits are retained within half the reusable quota, at most 16 results.
Sliders, tools, crop and layer gestures preempt optional folder work; obsolete recipes are cancelled and interactive drafts are not persisted.
Pause, cancellation, source changes, memory pressure and small/disabled cache preserve correct state and canonical pixels.

earlier_negative_runs.cause: Initial diagnostic seeded recipes while normal work had begun and used order-dependent exposure; excessive preparation and warm reuse failure. Also native edited results were retained too briefly. Diagnostic and retention corrected.
Warm background run recomputed one reduced edit during a short writer lock. Bounded cancellable retry added; final background case reuses every edit.

limits: Two copied real inputs (JPEG and Nikon D750 NEF), not a thousand-photo or all-camera qualification.
Preparation shifts cost to opening and consumes lossless disk space. Quotas can evict data; 100% does not guarantee simultaneous residency of the entire catalogue.
Future edits require new computation; adaptive drafts converge to canonical quality after the gesture. Heavy tools/layers have separate measured cadence.
Readiness and gesture timings refer to native software draw commands, not physical monitor latency or guaranteed frame rate.
The first background preparation overlapped a Rust test compilation; its loading time is observational, not a controlled performance comparison.
No macOS/XPC/Apple RAW validation and no R0-R4 or SF gate closure in this Windows campaign.
